title: Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM): who gets which Viva feature?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the policy controls, precedence, licensing prerequisite and limits. All twelve control surfaces were checked, and the open questions stay within the gaps in the documentation.

claims.claim: The on/off access setting is reached through Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select the Access setting option

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false and Everyone creates a tenant-wide disabling policy.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone

claims.claim: A policy's audience is set under Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Apply access settings to > Specific people and groups.
claims.quote: Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select Everyone or Specific people and groups under Apply access settings to. If you didn't select Everyone, add the specific people and groups you want to apply the policy to.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false, GroupIds and UserIds creates a disabling policy for the specified groups and UPNs.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com,57680382-61a5-4378-85ad-f72095d4e9c3 -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.claim: Supported features' user opt-out option is at Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting.
claims.quote: Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature. Some features also allow the option for users to opt out.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $true and IsUserControlEnabled $true enables a feature with user opt-out.
claims.quote: The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: $true: The feature is enabled by the policy. $true: User control is enabled by the policy. Users can opt out of the feature.

claims.claim: Existing policies can be edited at Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > More actions > Edit policy.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select the vertical ellipses (More actions) and choose Edit policy. Edit the desired fields.

claims.claim: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, PolicyId and GroupIds changes an existing policy's audience.
claims.quote: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com

claims.claim: Policies can be removed at Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > policy > Delete policy.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select the policy you'd like to delete. Select Delete policy.

claims.claim: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId and PolicyId deletes the specified policy.
claims.quote: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard policy path is Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights > Set up and management > Access Management > Turn Advanced Insights on or off > Feature access management > Agent Dashboard > Add policy.
claims.quote: go to the Set up and management tab. Under Access Management, select Turn Advanced Insights on or off. On the Feature access management page, select Agent Dashboard and Add policy.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId AgentDashboard -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the Agent Dashboard tenant-wide.
claims.quote:
Example: Turn off the Agent Dashboard for all users in your tenant
ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : AgentDashboard
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone

claims.claim: VFAM policies enable or disable specific Microsoft 365 and Viva features or types of data processing for users and groups in a tenant.
claims.quote: To control access to specific Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Viva features, you can create and update policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in PowerShell. You use policies to enable or disable specific features or types of data processing for users and groups in your tenant.

claims.claim: VFAM controls features in Viva Insights and Viva Pulse, including the Viva Insights web app and Agent Dashboard.
claims.quote:
Insights | Agent Dashboard | No | Global admin or AI admin | Viva Insights
Viva Insights web app | No | Global admin | Viva Insights
Pulse | Customization | No | Viva Pulse admin | Viva Pulse

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: ModuleId identifies the app module, with VivaInsights and VivaPulse as example module IDs.
claims.quote:
App | ModuleID
Insights | VivaInsights
Pulse | VivaPulse

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: FeatureId identifies the feature within the module.
claims.quote: The FeatureId parameter specifies the feature in the Viva module that you want to add the policy for.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A policy includes an enabled or disabled setting.
claims.quote: The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: $true: The feature is enabled by the policy. $false: The feature is not enabled by the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Policies can target everyone, groups or individual users.
claims.quote: Policies are used to restrict or grant access to the specified feature for specific users, groups, or the entire tenant.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind enables a feature for everyone in scope without considering user preference.
claims.quote: Admins can create the following policies, subject to feature support: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope without considering user preference.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind disables a feature for everyone in scope without considering user preference.
claims.quote: Disable the feature for everyone in the policy scope without considering user preference.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: One supported policy kind enables a feature while allowing users to opt out.
claims.quote: Enable the feature for everyone in the policy scope while providing users the ability to opt out.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Soft disable enables a feature with everyone in scope opted out by default but able to opt in, subject to feature support.
claims.quote: Enable the feature by opting out everyone in policy scope by default, while providing users the ability to opt in (soft disable). Some features don't support opt-out user controls or soft disable policies for admins to activate.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center and Exchange Online PowerShell manage VFAM access policies.
claims.quote: Policies can be created and managed by an admin who has permissions to do so in the Microsoft 365 admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Governance controls: Other surfaces
claims.claim: Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center also manage Viva Copilot policies and remain in sync with the VFAM admin page.
claims.quote: You can manage Copilot policies through Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. These policies remain in sync with policies managed through the admin page.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft's feature table lists the module, managing role and user opt-out support for each listed feature.
claims.quote: App | Feature | Control for user opt-out? | Who can manage access | ModuleID

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: Some VFAM features support tenant-wide policies only.
claims.quote: Some features only support policies that apply to the entire tenant, not specific users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The documented settings also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics where applicable.
claims.quote: The settings described below also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview) where applicable.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Agent 365 Business Analytics is identified as a Frontier preview.
claims.quote: Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview)

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: A user has one effective policy for each feature.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each feature.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins; Risks and limits: A narrower policy can undo a tenant-wide one
claims.claim: A policy assigned to a user or group takes priority over the tenant-wide policy.
claims.quote: Policies assigned to a specific user or group take priority over the policy assigned to the entire tenant when determining whether a feature is enabled.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Users in nested groups receive access policies applied to the parent group.
claims.quote: When users are in nested groups and you apply access policies to the parent group, the users in the nested groups receive the policies.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: The nested groups and their users must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: The nested groups and the users in those nested groups must be created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Without a user or group policy, the org-wide policy applies, which can be the feature default or an admin-created tenant policy.
claims.quote: If a user isn't assigned a policy as an individual or member of a group, the org-wide policy applies. It can be the default setting for the feature or a tenant-wide/org-wide policy created by the admin.

claims.where: What it is: Which policy wins
claims.claim: Within a single policy scope level, the most restrictive enablement policy takes precedence.
claims.quote: Then within a single Policy Scope Level, the most restrictive Enablement Policy takes precedence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: A narrower policy can undo a tenant-wide one
claims.claim: A custom user or group policy can allow access when organization-wide access is turned off.
claims.quote: Custom policies take precedence over your org-wide settings. For example, if you have organization-wide access turned off, a custom policy could still allow access for specific users or groups.

claims.claim: Default settings belong to individual features rather than being one universal VFAM default.
claims.quote: It can be the default setting for the feature or a tenant-wide/org-wide policy created by the admin.

claims.claim: Microsoft's VFAM feature table does not list default states.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva feature access management feature table default state. Opened https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management; read the complete feature table, whose columns are App, Feature, Control for user opt-out?, Who can manage access, ModuleID.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app is on by default, so no overriding policy leaves this default on.
claims.quote: The Viva Insights web app is on by default.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: The Agent Dashboard is on by default as part of the Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: Policy creation requires a supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.
claims.quote: Policy creation requires the following elements: A supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.

claims.claim: Microsoft links its Viva pricing page from the VFAM licensing requirement.
claims.quote: A [supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-viva/pricing).

claims.claim: The VFAM pages publish no separate price or meter for creating or holding policies at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Feature Access Management policy creation pricing meter charge. Read learn.microsoft.com/viva/feature-access-management, /viva/manage-access-policies and /viva/control-access-admin-center in full; they give prerequisites and policy limits but no separate policy price or meter.

claims.claim: A policy cannot grant access to a feature otherwise unavailable to the tenant, with EDU tenants as Microsoft's example.
claims.quote: You can control access to features that support access policies in your tenant. For example, if you have an EDU-based tenant, you can't use policies to gain access to features that aren't otherwise available to EDU tenants.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: UserIds, GroupIds or Everyone values on a policy update overwrite the existing audience.
claims.quote: Values that you specify for the -UserIds and -GroupIds parameters or the -Everyone parameter overwrite any existing users or groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Updates overwrite the audience
claims.claim: An audience update that omits existing users or groups removes those members from the policy.
claims.quote: Not including existing users or groups in the command effectively removes those specific users or groups from the policy.

claims.claim: Each feature permits a maximum of ten policies assigned to users and groups.
claims.quote: You can assign a maximum of 10 policies per feature to users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: A policy can cover a maximum of twenty total users or groups.
claims.quote: You can specify a maximum of 20 total users or groups (20 users and no groups, 10 users and 10 groups, etc.).

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Small limits
claims.claim: Each feature permits one additional tenant-wide policy using Everyone.
claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.

claims.claim: Policy names must be unique.
claims.quote: Policy names must be unique.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Access policy changes take effect within twenty-four hours unless a feature documents otherwise.
claims.quote: Changes to access policies take effect for the user within 24 hours, unless noted for a specific feature.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Copilot in Viva Engage access policy changes might take up to forty-eight hours.
claims.quote: Changes for Copilot in Viva Engage might take up to 48 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Changes are not immediate
claims.claim: Group membership changes can take twenty-four hours to affect feature access.
claims.quote: When you add users or remove them from a Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft 365 Group, it can take 24 hours before changes to their feature access take effect.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset
claims.claim: Fully enabling or disabling a feature resets the user's opt-in or opt-out preference to the default.
claims.quote: When an admin fully enables or disables a feature, the user's opt in/out preference resets to the default state.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Opt-out choices reset; What to check
claims.claim: Changes less than twenty-four hours apart might not reset user preferences, and Microsoft says to avoid such successive changes.
claims.quote: Avoid making changes to the enablement state for a feature less than 24 hours after making an initial change. Quick successive changes might not reset user opt in/out preferences.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleting user identities in Microsoft Entra ID deletes their data from VFAM.
claims.quote: When you delete user identities in Microsoft Entra ID, user data is also deleted from Viva feature access management.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Policies must be reassigned when a deleted user is re-enabled during the soft-deleted period.
claims.quote: If user identities are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Deleted Microsoft Entra ID groups are removed from stored VFAM policies.
claims.quote: When groups in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 are deleted, they're deleted from the stored policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Deleted identities lose policies
claims.claim: Policies must be reassigned when deleted groups are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period.
claims.quote: If groups are re-enabled during the soft-deleted period, the admin needs to reassign policies to the groups.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scope depends on the feature
claims.claim: User or group policies for Viva Insights web app auto-enablement are unsupported and have no effect.
claims.quote: This control supports tenant-level policies only, not user or group-level policies. User- and group-level policies aren't supported for this feature and will not take effect if used.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Turning off the Viva Insights web app disables the entire app, including the Copilot Dashboard.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: One switch can cover an app
claims.claim: Earlier configurations removing Copilot Dashboard access now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: If you previously removed access to the Copilot Dashboard using Copilot Dashboard feature access management control or PowerShell, those configurations now apply to the entire Viva Insights web app.

claims.claim: The documented access controls are unavailable in GCC High and DoD, with GCC availability referred to individual app documentation.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD. For GCC (Government Community Cloud), see the documentation for your specific app for availability.

claims.claim: Running the policy cmdlets requires Global Administrators membership or a role assigned at feature level.
claims.quote: Currently, you need to be a member of the Global Administrators role or the roles that have been assigned at the feature level to run this cmdlet.

claims.claim: The feature table names Global admin or AI admin as the managing roles for Agent Dashboard.
claims.quote: Insights | Agent Dashboard | No | Global admin or AI admin | Viva Insights

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends least privilege rather than routine Global Administrator use.
claims.quote: Microsoft strongly advocates for the principle of least privilege. Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that you typically limit to emergency scenarios or when you can't use a different role.

claims.claim: IsUserControlEnabled can be used only for features that allow admins to toggle user controls.
claims.quote: Only features that allow admins to enable and disable user controls by policy can use this parameter.

claims.claim: Adding IsUserOptedInByDefault $false to an enabled policy with user controls sets soft disable.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId PeopleSkills -FeatureId ShowAISkills -Name SoftDisableShowAISkillsPolicy -IsFeatureEnabled $true -IsUserControlEnabled $true -IsUserOptedInByDefault $false -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.claim: IsUserOptedInByDefault requires IsUserControlEnabled $true.
claims.quote: This parameter can be set only when the IsUserControlEnabled parameter is set to $true.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app is a VFAM feature with FeatureId 'Viva Insights web app'.
claims.quote:
ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : Viva Insights web app
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone

claims.where: Governance controls: Other surfaces; What to check
claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature lists the features in a module that support access policies and their identifiers.
claims.quote: Use the Get-VivaModuleFeature PowerShell cmdlet to get a list of all of the features available in a specific Microsoft 365 app and their associated IDs. Run the Get-VivaModuleFeature cmdlet to see the features that you can manage by using an access policy.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls: Other surfaces; What to check
claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy views existing feature policies and returns their policy IDs.
claims.quote: start by getting the specific UID for the access policy - you can get that by running Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement returns the enablement status for a user or group.
claims.quote: To check what features are disabled for a specific user or group, run the Get-VivaModuleFeatureEnablement cmdlet. This cmdlet returns what's called the enablement status for the user or group.

claims.claim: Microsoft points to VFAM change logs in Microsoft Purview for policy creation, updates and deletions.
claims.quote: For a history of policy creation, updates, and deletions, see the Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) change logs for your organization in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: The VFAM PowerShell requirements specify Exchange Online PowerShell 3.2.0 or later.
claims.quote: Access to Exchange Online PowerShell Version 3.2.0 or later.

claims.claim: The VFAM requirements specify Exchange PowerShell 3.5.1 or later for non-mail-enabled groups.
claims.quote: If you need to use non-mail-enabled groups you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.5.1 or later.

claims.claim: The VFAM requirements specify Exchange PowerShell 3.8.0 or later for soft-disable policies.
claims.quote: If you need to setup policies with the user opted-out by default (soft-disable), you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.8.0 or later.

claims.claim: The Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy reference specifies module 3.8.0-Preview2 or later for IsUserOptedInByDefault.
claims.quote: This parameter is available in module version 3.8.0-Preview2 or later.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph or REST operation for managing VFAM policies was found in the November 2026 Learn search.
claims.quote: Searched: "VFAM" "REST" "Graph" policies. Read VFAM overview and PowerShell guide on Learn. Graph results document vfamCreatePolicyAuditRecord and vfamUpdatePolicyAuditRecord with Methods: None, not policy-management operations.

claims.claim: The VFAM pages point to Purview change logs without naming audit operations.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Feature Access Management VFAM audit log operation names policy creation update deletion Purview. Read /viva/feature-access-management and /viva/control-access-admin-center at learn.microsoft.com; they link or refer to change logs but list no operation names.

claims.claim: The admin center VFAM page does not mention soft disable, while the PowerShell pages document IsUserOptedInByDefault.
claims.quote: Searched: "VFAM" "soft disable" "admin center". Read learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center, /viva/manage-access-policies and the Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy reference; only the latter two describe soft disable.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is a public preview.
claims.quote: The Agent Dashboard is for public preview customers only. Features in preview might not be complete and could undergo changes before becoming available in the broader release.

claims.claim: The AI admin can enable or disable Agent Dashboard at tenant, group or user level.
claims.quote: The AI admin can enable or disable the Agent Dashboard at the tenant, group, or user level using the Agent Dashboard VFAM control in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Agent Dashboard access requires both its own control and the Viva Insights web app control to be enabled.
claims.quote: To access the Agent Dashboard, both the Viva Insights web app control and this control must be enabled.

claims.claim: The Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy Everyone switch must not be combined with GroupIds or UserIds.
claims.quote: Don't use this switch with the GroupIds or UserIds parameters.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app and Agent Dashboard report on employees' activity.
claims.quote: Your organization might want to exclude certain users from being included in the aggregated insights in the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Agent Dashboard, Consumption Dashboard, or Viva Insights behavior collaboration reports in advanced analysis for various reasons
